A few direct customers each buy a double-digit share of revenue (saved analysis customer_concentration), so a handful of buyers' capex plans can move the rent.
definition: NVIDIA's gross margin (gross profit ÷ revenue, whole company) by fiscal quarter from audited and reviewed SEC filings, as the cleanest public read on how much of the stack's surplus the chip layer keeps.

direction_rule.rationale: Four fiscal quarters; a move under one point of margin is noise. Rising margin = rent concentrating at the chip layer.

name: Rent concentration in semiconductors

status_events.author: claude-initial-seed
status_events.reason: NVIDIA gross margin by fiscal quarter from 10-K/10-Q XBRL: Apr 2025 60.5%, Jul 2025 72.4%, Oct 2025 73.4%, Apr 2026 74.9%, Jul 2026 75.0%. Four-quarter change exceeds the one-point dead band and every step is up. Whole-company margin; segment margins are not in the company-facts API. Initial seed.

timing_rationale: Lagging: chip margins reflect orders placed quarters earlier and are filed a quarter after they are earned.
tracker_interpretation: The margin has held at the level a monopolist would print. Custom silicon share and AMD's data-centre ramp are the things that would erode it.
why_it_matters: Nordhaus's base rate says innovators keep ~2% of surplus; a 70%+ gross margin at the bottom of the stack is the opposite pattern. Whether it holds, rises or erodes is the first capture question.
